I wanted to like this book more than I did. The premise is great: a lighthouse keeper in 1890s Maine starts receiving letters addressed to a wife he never had. For the first eighty pages I could not put it down. The fog, the oil smell, the supply boat that comes every second Thursday unless the weather says otherwise, all of that is done with real care.

Then the middle happens. There's a long stretch in Boston that reads like a different, worse novel got shuffled in by mistake. New characters show up, talk at length about shipping insurance, and vanish. I counted, and the keeper is absent for sixty-one pages of his own story.

It recovers. The last third goes back to the island and the ending is quiet and strange and I've thought about it most days since. I won't spoil it except to say the letters are explained and also not, and that felt right to me, though my book club was split four to three.

Three stars, but a weird three. I'd lend it to you and tell you which chapters to skim.
